note: Rewritten from the original description by Emerson (1928), the original in English; the holotype is a soldier (American Museum of Natural History) and the type locality is Niangara, Democratic Republic of the Congo (collected by Lang-Chapin, 20 May 1913 (month 5, day 20)). The alate and worker are not recorded. Synonymy citations, distribution and figure numbers have not been translated. In the excerpts, words broken at the ends of lines in the original have been joined.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head reddish yellow; sides straight and parallel, not narrowing forwards. Antennae 15—16-segmented, usually 16, in which case segment 4 is slightly shorter than segment 3 and segment 3 is shorter than segment 2. The eye spot behind the antennal base is invisible or extremely indistinct. When the mandibles are closed the labrum does not reach the teeth of the left mandible. Anterior margin of the pronotum deeply concave. Measurements (mm): head length 2.73—2.79, head width 1.28—1.35, pronotum length 0.48—0.51, pronotum width 0.93—0.96, tibia length 0.96, left mandible length 1.12.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: T. stercorivorus has proportionally greater head length; T. scrutor has indistinct mandibular teeth and less curved mandibular apices; T. badius is much larger.
